Earnings Call Transcript
Altria (MO) Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Apr 22, 2026 at 4:34PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


DATE
Thursday, October 31, 2024 at 9:00 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
Chief Executive Officer — Billy Gifford
Chief Financial Officer — Sal Mancuso
Vice President, Investor Relations — Mac Livingston
TAKEAWAYS
Adjusted Diluted EPS
-- Grew by 7.8% in the quarter and by 1.6% in the first nine months; full-year guidance reaffirmed at $5.07 to $5.15, representing 2.5%-4% growth from $4.95 in 2023.
Smokable Products Segment Adjusted OCI
-- Increased 7.1% in the quarter and 0.9% year-to-date; margins expanded to 63.1% in the quarter.
Smokable Products Net Price Realization
-- Achieved 10.6% quarterly and 9.7% year-to-date net price realization.
Domestic Cigarette Volume
-- Reported volumes declined 8.6% in the quarter; adjusted for trade and calendar effects, volumes decreased 11.5% in the quarter.
Marlboro Premium Segment Share
-- Expanded to 59.3%, adding 0.3 share points year over year.
NJOY Consumables Shipment Volume
-- Increased more than 15% to 10.4 million units; device shipment volume nearly tripled to 1.1 million units.
NJOY Retail Share
-- Achieved 6.2 share points, up 2.8 points year over year and 0.8 sequentially.
NJOY Net Promoter Score
-- Surpassed prior year by over 20 points.
On! Oral Nicotine Pouch Shipment Volume
-- Grew 46% to nearly 42 million cans.
On! Repeat Purchasers
-- Repeat purchases increased 40% to around 700,000 consumers; contributed over 80% of third-quarter on! volume.
Oral Tobacco Products Segment Adjusted OCI
-- Rose by 2% in the quarter with margins at 66.8%; volume increased 1.2% but adjusted volume declined about 1% in the period.
Oral Tobacco Products Segment Retail Share
-- Fell by 4.2 points in the quarter as MST brand declines were partially offset by on! gains.
ABI Investment Adjusted Equity Earnings
-- Recorded $144 million for the quarter, up 0.7% year over year, reflecting reduced ownership after a prior partial sale.
Dividends and Share Repurchases
-- Paid $1.7 billion in dividends and repurchased 13.5 million shares for $680 million; remaining $310 million under repurchase authorization expected to be completed by year-end.
Cost-Savings Initiative
-- Initial phases targeting at least $600 million in cumulative savings over five years, with $100 million to $125 million pretax charges, mostly excluded from adjusted EPS.
Debt to EBITDA Ratio
-- Reported at 2.1x as of September 30, in line with target levels.
Patent Litigation Timeline
-- ITC final determination in Juul's case against NJOY expected by late December, with a second final determination in early April.
Illicit Product Market Estimates
-- E-vapor illicit disposable user base grew 45% to 12.4 million adults; over 1,000 illicit nicotine pouch SKUs identified at retail and online.
Youth Tobacco Use Trends
-- Achieved all Healthy People 2030 adolescent usage reduction goals; referenced ongoing regulatory and enforcement challenges.

[email protected]
RISKS
Sal Mancuso stated, "smokers remain under economic pressure as the cumulative impacts from prolonged inflation persist and constrain discretionary income."
Category volume declines in cigarettes were described as "elevated partly due to the growth of illicit flavored disposable e-vapor products and continued discretionary income pressures on consumers."
Management cited more than 1,000 illicit nicotine pouch SKUs on the market and described the FDA’s enforcement actions as inadequate, creating "confusion among legitimate manufacturers."
Patent litigation with Juul could create product import disruptions, with the CEO noting, "an exclusion order would go into effect" if the ITC decision favors Juul and Presidential appeal is unsuccessful.
SUMMARY
Altria Group

(
MO

+2.03%
)
reported higher adjusted diluted EPS and reaffirmed its full-year outlook, with performance driven by smokable segment margin expansion and pricing actions. The company highlighted significant growth in its NJOY vapor and on! oral nicotine pouch brands, including notable improvements in shipment volume and consumer loyalty. Management reiterated plans to deliver $600 million in multi-year cost savings through process modernization and confirmed the timeline for ITC decisions in ongoing Juul patent litigation.
Federal tax settlements related to Juul allowed Altria to recognize $4 billion in ordinary and $4.1 billion in capital losses, with $3.2 billion in realized offset against gains and $5.6 billion in capital losses carried forward for future use, though none of the $5.6 billion is recognized for financial reporting.
The smokable segment's discount share rose 1.5 points during the quarter, and cigarette industry volume declines were attributed partly to consumer downtrading under economic stress.
Marlboro's retail share of the cigarette category decreased both year over year and sequentially, even as it gained share within the premium segment.
Management expects extra shipping days in both Q3 and Q4 to impact shipment volumes but noted these effects typically balance out over time.
The company emphasized ongoing engagement with the FDA and legislators regarding regulatory actions affecting e-vapor and nicotine pouch segments.
A joint venture with Japan Tobacco for the Ploom heated tobacco device is progressing, with regulatory filings anticipated in the first half of 2025.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
OCI (Operating Companies Income)
: Segment-level operating profit excluding certain nonrecurring items, used as a measure of underlying business profitability.
Net Price Realization
: The net impact of price changes on revenue after accounting for promotional spending, discounts, and allowances.
PMTA (Premarket Tobacco Product Application)
: Regulatory submission required for FDA authorization to market new tobacco products in the U.S.
MSA (Master Settlement Agreement)
: A legal settlement dictating certain payments and restrictions for cigarette manufacturers in the U.S.
SE (Substantial Equivalence) Application
: FDA filing asserting that a new or modified tobacco product is substantially equivalent to an already authorized predicate product.
MST (Moist Smokeless Tobacco)
: A category of oral tobacco products including premium and value dip brands.
